title: Consolidate input density and surface token mappings across text fields, selects, and toggles
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Context: Over the last two quarters we shipped individual tweaks to text fields, selects, and toggles to meet product use-cases (compact mode, high-contrast mode, and dense table rows). Those changes were implemented in isolation and have created inconsistent surface token mappings (elevation, background, focus ring, stroke, and spacing) across components. This causes visual drift across pages and increases engineering QA burden when changing tokens.

Goal: Create a single, well-documented mapping between design surface tokens and form component states (default, hover, focus, active, disabled, invalid) across text fields, selects, and toggles. Reduce token variance so a single theme apply produces consistent visuals in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope:
- Audit current token usage across text field variants (default, leading/trailing icons, multiline), select components (single, multi, searchable), and toggle/switch states.
- Propose a canonical mapping table that ties component states to surface tokens (background, stroke, focus, shadow) for three density modes: default, compact, and dense-table.
- Update Figma component library and tokens file.
- Implement a clear migration guide for engineers (token names to change, recommended aliases to preserve backward compatibility).
- Add automated screenshot regressions in the component test harness for the three densities.

Acceptance criteria:
- Single mapping table merged into design tokens doc and referenced in component specs.
- Figma components updated and verified in two product pages (Console forms + onboarding).
- PR to the component library includes token aliases so existing usages do not break and feature-flag guard for rollout.
- Unit/regression visual tests added and green in CI.
- Engineering sign-off from ENG-4321 and accessibility sign-off confirming contrast and focus behavior.

Success metrics:
- Reduction of cross-team UI issues related to input visuals by 50% in the next quarter.
- Faster PR review time for form UI changes (measured by mean time from PR open to merge) down by 25% for related repos.
comments: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Confluence. Agreement from frontend and infra to use token aliases during migration. Links: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Inputs+Token+Audit

2026-02-28: Audit complete — attached spreadsheet lists 42 token usages across components. Observations: focus stroke values vary between 1px and 2px, dense-table mode was implemented by shrinking padding only (no token changes).

2026-03-02: Design decision: use surface.token.input.background.{default|compact|dense} and surface.token.input.stroke.* pattern. Chosen to minimize churn in SDKs. Recorded in PRD: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/inputs-prd

2026-03-05: Engineering review (ENG-4321) — requested alias layer for legacy tokens and a feature-flagged rollout. Frontend estimate: 5 dev days + 2 QA days. Added ENG-4455 to handle visual regression pipeline updates.

2026-03-08: Accessibility review: tab focus size and contrast verified for default and compact tokens; dense-table requires a slight stroke contrast bump for WCAG AA with 12px text. Action: update dense stroke token value and re-run tests.
2026-03-10: Figma update in progress. Link to updated component variants: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/Design-System-Inputs?node-id=234:0
2026-03-11: Draft migration guide uploaded — includes list of token renames and recommended aliases. Link to migration doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Inputs+Token+Migration

2026-03-12: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/components/pull/782 — includes token alias layer, updated text-field/select/toggle stories, and visual test baseline updates. Waiting on ENG + QA review.
